title: Write the rules of a game you invent
description: Every game you love began as rules somebody wrote down. Invent a simple game, write its rules in a notebook, and test whether a friend can play it from your words alone.
author: SparkKindly · AI-assisted

body.heading: Start with a tiny game
paragraphs: Pick something small: a card game with ten cards, a race game on a drawn track, or a guessing game with three rules. Give it a name and write down the goal in one sentence — what does a player have to do to win?
Then write the setup (what each player starts with) and the turn order (what one player does on their turn). Three to five rules is plenty for a first version.

body.heading: The real test: hand over the notebook
paragraphs: Give your written rules to a friend or family member and watch them play without explaining anything. Every question they ask shows a rule that is missing or unclear — write that rule down on the spot.
Change one rule at a time between games and note what happened. Game designers call this playtesting, and your notebook becomes the record of how your game grew from a rough idea into one that works.

takeaway: Invent a small game, write its goal, setup and turns in a notebook, then let a friend play from the words alone — their questions are your missing rules.
materials: A notebook or several sheets of paper
Simple props your game needs, such as cards, counters or dice
supervision: An adult or older sibling acts as the first playtester and helps the inventor word the rules clearly.
safetyNotes: Keep small game pieces away from very young children, who may put them in their mouths.
Playtest kindly — questions about the rules are help, not criticism of the inventor.
